notes: carBox/wheels read off the 2322x3542 pack photo with a pixel ruler: the black tyres sit on the dark bare-metal base, so the wheel circles are given rather than detected

sheet: only a DRAFT exists (reference-collector .../generated/draft-sheet.png, no accepted reference-sheet.png); the founder explicitly approved using it for this Tripo test. hints.json "sheet" points the ripcars commands at it (layout from the manifest's preview entry) while no accepted sheet exists; an accepted reference-sheet.png wins automatically once there is one
model.fit width 0.938: clean's per-axis fit left the body 1.066x the top drawing's width (Tripo never sees the top); this brings it to the sheet

model.glass replace all five views, no glass at all: the sheet's window finder took the white body/engine for glass and missed the canopies (qa glass.jpg). The canopies stay OPAQUE purple paint on purpose: on the toy they are purple-tinted clear plastic, but the app's glass (app/src/glass.ts) only draws a neutral dark-grey or near-black tint, so either glass mode would turn the car's signature magenta bubbles grey/black; Tripo's bubbles are also closed shells with no cockpit under them to see into

model.rebake.noalign top: the top drawing's alignment was weak (match 0.19, ~20 px median shift; Tripo never saw the top) and the warped paint came out washed out and ghosted on the engine, roundel and flames; projected straight instead

side_iou 0.896 / left_iou 0.893 gates (0.93 / 0.90) accepted: the misses are the same on both sides - the draft sheet's elevated side cameras show the engine deck and nose-pod tops above the true profile (Codex's review flags exactly this), so the drawn nose sits ~2% of length higher than Tripo's. The pack photo (real toy, level) agrees with Tripo's nose: landing IoU 0.91 with no doubled edges. Not a size problem, so no model.fit for it; an accepted level-camera sheet would settle it

model.glb 1.34 MB: it was 1.92 MB because rebake passed Tripo's normal map through untouched when a car has no glass to flatten (this one has none), and the export re-encoded it as a 644 KB PNG (not the metal/roughness map, which is 143 KB JPEG like the others). rebake now always writes the normal map as JPEG q92 (64 KB); mean change 1.2/255 per channel, no visible difference

model.push (2026-10-19, founder: 'doesn't match from above; the middle was too hard for Tripo, it had no knowledge of the top'): Tripo filled the gap between the nose pods with a flat centre plank running ~35 px (sheet top px) further forward than the drawing's notch (x 943 vs the drawn deck edge at x 904-915 between the pod tips at 981), and the engine's front pipes ran on to x 885 over the drawn deck where the roundel sits. Two top-view prisms slide those vertices back towards the tail (dir [-1, 0]): below 0.33 H the plank's front ends on the drawn notch curve; above 0.33 H the pipes end at x 838, just ahead of the drawn engine (front ~815), leaving the deck clear. Polygons span y 869-967 only, inside the pods' inner walls (862-866 / 971-977), so the pods, wheels and landing are untouched; the mesh stays closed (no holes). Top IoU 0.931 -> 0.942

model.rebake.material: the generator's metal map made the white body ~0.6 metallic and the canopies 1.0, so in the app the body read grey, the flames washed out and the canopies deep plum, while its engine was ~0.5 and read flat grey. Metallic 0 everywhere first; the engine (top prism around it, above 0.3 H) metallic 1 / roughness 0.25 so it reads as chrome like the drawing; the canopies metallic 0.6 / roughness 0.25 (0 came out pale pink on the compare page, 1 too dark: the painted texture is the drawing's magenta - only the lighting differed). Rectangles on the canopies from above are the room environment's light panels reflected, not paint

model.rebake.skip dropped, roundel follows the TOP drawing now (founder wants the car to match from above): the top drawing paints it on the centre deck between the pods (866,925), which model.push uncovered. The vehicle-left pod (840,825), where the front drawing and Tripo put it, is painted plain white by the top drawing; model.rebake.flat on that circle flattens Tripo's embossed normal-map relief there (a faint geometric ring stays). The canopies and flames needed no paint change: the bake already copies them crisply from the top drawing (noalign) - their faded look in the app was the metal map
